Question Choices: If y = 4x + 1 and y = 13 intersect, what is the x-coordinate of the solution?
Solution: Set the common outputs equal: 4x+(1)=13. Subtract 1 to get 4x=12, then divide by 4: x=3. The shared point is (3,13); substituting verifies both rules.

Hints: Solutions are shared points.;There are none.
Solution: A solution is a shared ordered pair on the graphs. The stated number of intersections is 0, hence there are 0 real solutions. For two functions y=f(x),y=g(x), each intersection gives one distinct input solving f(x)=g(x).

Solution: The shared point (2,7) means f(2)=7 and g(2)=7. Subtract to get f(2)-g(2)=7-7=0.
